root_cause_hypothesis: FIX-VERIFICATION RUN. Both headline TOOL_DEFECTs of the 2026-08-31 capture run (2026-08-31T22__L4-headerlines-document-slice__278eee3) are CONFIRMED FIXED by read-back from disk, and the two hand-repaired golden lines are now real captured bytes. REPRODUCTION 2 (DeleteAction) - FIXED AT THE ROOT. add-delete-action(deleteActionType Cascade, deleteActionRelation ConDemoRentHeader) wrote Name -> DeleteAction -> Relation -> Table, the canonical order of all shipped AxTableDeleteAction entries (verified against ApplicationSuite/Foundation/AxTable/SalesTable.xml, 15 entries, and CustAutomationStrategy.xml). TWO subsequent bridge-backed IMetadataProvider.Update() modifies on the SAME table (modify-property FormRef, then modify-property TitleField2) left the element intact, and it is still intact after a full rebuild. No restore guard fired for it - the provider now READS the element and writes it back itself, which is a root fix rather than a compensation. REPRODUCTION 1 (CacheLookup) - COMPENSATED, NOT ROOT-FIXED. create(table ConDemoRentLine, cacheLookup None) again reported: Written after the create (the metadata writer dropped it): <CacheLookup>None</CacheLookup> - i.e. the TS layer still patches the file. The next bridge-backed modify (add-relation) then reported, VERBATIM: Restored after the write: CacheLookup=None. The metadata round trip dropped it - an element this operation never touched. Put back from the pre-write file rather than left to disappear silently; re-read the object if you need to be sure of its current shape. The value survives on disk (confirmed by grep after the modify and again after the full build), so the observable defect is gone, but the underlying provider round trip STILL DROPS CacheLookup and is now corrected after the fact. That guard is load-bearing: any future write path that does not run it re-opens the bug, and a restore-from-pre-write-file cannot distinguish a round trip that dropped the element from a caller that meant to clear it. NEW KNOWLEDGE_GAP (documentation defect in the very parameter this run was asked to exercise): get_knowledge(kind=op-spec, topic=add-delete-action) documents deleteActionRelation as: Relation on THIS table that the delete action follows. That is backwards. Every shipped example puts the relation of the RELATED (child) table there - the CustAutomationStrategy delete action on table CustAutomationStrategyLine carries <Relation>CustAutomationStrategy</Relation>, which is the relation defined ON CustAutomationStrategyLine pointing back at the parent. This run passed ConDemoRentHeader (the relation on ConDemoRentLine) on that AOT evidence rather than on the op-spec text; an agent following the op-spec literally would look for a relation on the header table, find only CustTable, and either pass the wrong name or omit the parameter and keep the BPUpgradeMetadataDeleteAction warning. UNFIXED KNOWLEDGE_GAP (re-reported from the previous run suggested_fix_area item 4): get_knowledge(kind=op-spec, topic=scaffold:form) STILL omits linesTable and linesDataSource from its optional list. They remain the only way to get a correct DetailsTransaction lines datasource, and passing linesTable again produced a form byte-identical to the golden. An agent following the documented contract still gets the 2026-07-07 outcome: a fabricated datasource and a build failure. UNFIXED VALIDATOR_GAP: object_patterns(action=validate, formName=ConDemoRentAgreement) again passed with 0 errors and 3 FP002 warnings (its own generator FieldsFieldGroups PatternVersion 1.1 is older than the catalog 1.2), while xppbp then raised 5 BPErrorLabelIsText on tab Captions the scaffold itself wrote as raw text plus BPCheckPassiveJoinUse on the datasource the scaffold itself bound. UNFIXED TOOL_DEFECT (BP defaults): d365fo_file(create, table) still leaves 5 preventable BP warnings - BPErrorTablePrimaryKeyEditable x3 (it sets ReplacementKey/AlternateKey but never AllowEdit=No on the key fields) and BPErrorDeveloperDocumentationNotDefined x2 (developerDocumentation is still absent from the create contract). NEW TOOL_DEFECT (corpus fidelity, low severity): src/eval/oracle/cli.ts --bp-warnings <N> writes N EMPTY objects into build.bpWarnings[]. The record it produced carried thirteen empty braces, so every BP code this run measured would be invisible to eval:clusters and eval:brief. The previous run ORACLE DEFECT (empty generated_artifacts on a capture run) IS fixed, but the list is now filled with golden filenames such as ConDemoRentHeader.metadata.xml where the schema asks for AOT paths and every earlier record uses AxTable/ConDemoRentHeader.xml; both fields were corrected by hand in this record. NEW TOOL_DEFECT (low severity, prepare): prepare(mode=create) has no enum-extension objectType. Asking it about NumberSeqModule.ConDemoRent as objectType=enum returns a hard error line - Name may contain only letters, digits and underscores, and must not start with a digit - plus the suggestion ConNumberSeqModule.ConDemoRent, a name that would be wrong. The grounding token it issued was accepted by the enum-extension create, so the guidance is wrong while the plumbing is right. NEW ENV/INDEX observation (rollback hygiene, not a case failure): after the previous run rollback the ConDemo label file was absent from disk while the symbol index still answered labels(action=info, labelId=@ConDemo:RentModule) with a full hit including model, label file and comment. labels(action=create, createIfMissing=true) nevertheless wrote all 10 labels and the AxLabelFile pair to disk, so nothing broke - but a stale label index can make an agent skip a create it actually needs.
